# Apps {#sec-apps}

```{r}
#| include: false
# knitr evaluates inline `r ...` only in a document that has at least one code
# chunk; the app links below are doc_app_url()/doc_atlas_url() calls (they
# follow this release's host and version), so without this they would print
# as literal text.
```

The MST provides three interactive web applications — two Shiny apps (Scores, Species) plus a newer, static, in-browser Atlas — along with several legacy applications from earlier development phases.

::: {.callout-note}
## One application, every release

Every one of the three current apps renders **any published release** rather than shipping a per-version fork. Scores and Species do this from the URL (`/v3/scores/`; older `?ver=v3` links redirect there) — the version is data, settled by the release's published manifest, so a fix reaches every version at once, and the 18 former per-version Shiny instances are retired with their URLs redirecting permanently to the equivalent path. The Atlas follows the same rule with a different mechanism (@sec-app-atlas): one static build reads the same published `versions.json`, resolving the release from `?ver=` on its public host, and — once its preview route ships — from the URL path on its signed-in preview host.
:::

These tools allow stakeholders, scientists, and decision-makers to understand the underlying components contributing to an area's sensitivity to offshore energy development, supporting better planning and impact assessment.

## Current Applications

### Atlas (beta) — static, in-browser scores, species and places

The [Atlas](`r doc_atlas_url()`) is a newer, third way to explore the MST, currently labelled
**beta**: one static Svelte/MapLibre app with **no application server of its own** — scores,
clicks, flowers and reports are computed in your browser by a DuckDB-WASM instance, though score
tiles, zone outlines and the basemap still come from the project's titiler, PMTiles and CARTO.
It combines what Scores and Species do separately — mapping composite scores and mapping
individual species — with a capability neither Shiny app has, **Places**: drawing, typing or
uploading any area of interest (not only the built-in Program Areas) and getting the same scores,
species tables and an exportable report for it, shareable entirely through the URL.

See @sec-app-atlas for the full walkthrough, including how a drawn place is encoded into a shareable link.

### Scores — mapper of aggregate sensitivity scores

The [Scores](`r doc_app_url("scores")`) application is the primary tool for exploring composite sensitivity scores across BOEM Program Areas. Key features include:

- **Multi-resolution viewing**: toggle between cell-level (0.05° grid) and Program Area aggregations
- **Study area selection**: focus on specific Program Areas or subregions
- **Layer selection**: view individual species category scores or composite metrics
- **Flower plot**: interactive summary showing scores by species category with weighted center value
- **Species table**: sortable table of species present in selected area with extinction risk details
- **Treemap**: hierarchical view of species contributions to sensitivity
- **CSV export**: download data for selected area or species

Under the hood the Scores app composes three kinds of map layer (@fig-architecture):

- **Score raster** — a pre-rendered COG per metric × subregion, whose URL and rescale range come straight from the release manifest. The browser fetches only the tiles intersecting its viewport; no full-raster transfer on load (see @fig-raster).
- **"Cells outside Program Areas" mask** — a single-color overlay published the same way.
- **Zone choropleth** — polygon geometry from a static PMTiles archive published per geometry **vintage**, with per-zone fill colors pushed live into the paint spec from the release's `zone_metric` (see @fig-choropleth).

Because every one of those is resolved from the manifest rather than hardcoded, switching the URL's version segment (e.g. `/v3/` → `/v4/`) switches all three together — including drawing the boundary vintage that release actually used.

See @sec-app-scores for details.

### Species — mapper of individual species distributions

The [Species](`r doc_app_url("species")`) application enables exploration of individual species distribution models. Key features include:

- **Species selection**: search by common or scientific name, filter by species category
- **Model display**: view merged models or individual source dataset layers
- **Representation toggle**: compare the native-resolution original with the interpolated surface used in scoring
- **Masking toggle**: compare the expert-range-constrained merged model with the unconstrained suitability
- **Species info panel**: ESA listing, IUCN Red List category, MMPA/MBTA protection flags, extinction risk score
- **Deep-linking**: URL parameters support direct links to specific species

See @sec-app-species for details.

## Legacy Applications

Earlier prototype applications from the research phase are kept in the Appendix under Applications (Legacy) for reference. They are not part of the current serving path.
